master.title: There is chance to agree with U.S., NATO on key proposals on security guarantees - Lavrov; Putin backs continuation of talks on security guarantees with West
master.content:
Reply to U.S., NATO's reaction to Russian security proposals formulated - Lavrov

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - The Russian Foreign Ministry has drafted a response to the replies given by the United States and NATO to the Russian proposals on security guarantees, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said.

"It has been formulated on ten pages," Lavrov said at a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Monday.

Lavrov describes replies to Russia's request regarding indivisible security interpretation as unsatisfactory

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - The responses received by Russia following its request regarding the interpretation of the principle of indivisible security are unsatisfactory, and Moscow will continue seeking a specific reaction from each country at the national level, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said.

"The replies that I have received are unsatisfactory. None of my counterparts have responded to my direct message. We have received two small pieces of paper: one from NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg and the other from EU diplomacy chief Josep Borrell. They say: 'don't worry, it's necessary to continue dialogue, the main thing you should do is to ensure de-escalation around Ukraine'," Lavrov said at a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Monday.

There is chance to agree with U.S., NATO on key proposals on security guarantees - Lavrov

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Russia is unwilling to talk endlessly with the United States and NATO on key security issues of concern to Moscow, but there is a chance to reach agreements, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said.

"We have said more than once that we warn against endless conversations on issues that need to be resolved today, but still, probably as the foreign minister, I should say that there is always a chance," Lavrov said at a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Putin backs continuation of talks on security guarantees with West

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Russian President Vladimir Putin has backed the continuation of consultations with the West on security issues of concern to Russia.

During a meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov on Monday, the president asked him if there was a chance to agree with the West on key issues of concern to Russia or if this was an attempt to drag Russia into endless talks.

"You have said, and other Russian representatives have said, that we warn against endless conversations on issues that need to be resolved today. Still, as the foreign minister, I should say that there is always a chance," Lavrov said.

"It seems to me that our possibilities are far from being exhausted. They certainly should not continue indefinitely, but at this stage I would suggest that they continue and be intensified," he said.

"All right," Putin said.

Shoigu briefs Putin on military exercises

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - Russian Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu is briefing President Vladimir Putin about military exercises, including those in southern Russia and those held jointly with Belarus.

"Sergei Kuzhugetovich, I know you are now ready to report on the course of the exercises we are conducting in various parts of the World Ocean: in the Far East, in the South, in the North, in the Central Military District, and with our friends in Belarus," Putin said at their meeting on Monday.

"I am listening to you," he added.

Russian military holding exercises in almost all fleets, military districts - Shoigu

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - The Russian military is conducting exercises in practically all fleets and military districts, some of them are nearing completion, Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu said.

"Exercises are being held by the Western Military District, virtually in all fleets, including those in the Barents Sea, the Black Sea, the Baltic Sea, and the Pacific Fleet. Troops from almost all military districts are taking part in them," Shoigu said at a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"Some of these exercises are about to be completed, some will be completed in the near future," the minister said.

Kremlin points to Ukrainian forces' redeployment near contact line with DPR and LPR

MOSCOW. Feb 14 (Interfax) - The Kremlin has brought to notice large-scale redeployments of Ukrainian Armed Forces personnel in the proximity of the line of contact with the self-proclaimed Donetsk (DPR) and Luhansk (LPR) People's Republics, a circumstance which the Kremlin believes adds to tension.

"I want to repeat once again about Russian forces' relocations within the territory of the Russian Federation. There are equally large-scale relocations of the Armed Forces of Ukraine and various units of different types ongoing both in the border area and in Ukrainian territory bordering the territory of the self-proclaimed republics, thus, of course, leading to a serious deterioration of the situation," Russian presidential press secretary Dmitry Peskov said when asked by reporters whether Russia plans to give Kyiv a response regarding Russian troops' redeployment in the border area, and how the Kremlin is treating Kyiv's request to convene a meeting with Russia and other signatories to the 2011 Vienna Document.

Peskov declined to further comment on this matter.

OSCE meeting on situation near Ukrainian border with Russia scheduled for Feb 15 - Poland's OSCE chairmanship

BERLIN. Feb 14 (Interfax) - An Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) meeting requested by Kyiv to discuss Russian troops' redeployment near the border with Ukraine will be held on Tuesday, February 15, the Polish OSCE chairmanship said on Twitter.

"Ukraine requested the Polish OSCE Chairmanship to hold a meeting with Russia and other interested states with regard to unusual military activities. The meeting will be convened on Tuesday in accordance with Vienna Document," Poland's OSCE chairmanship said on Twitter on Monday.

The Ukrainian Foreign Ministry said earlier on Monday that the meeting should take place "probably on February 15."

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba said the day before that Ukraine was convening such a meeting.

"Russia failed to respond to our request under the Vienna Document. Consequently, we are taking the next step. We request a meeting with Russia and all participating states within 48 hours to discuss its reinforcement and redeployment along our border," Kuleba said on Twitter.

candidate.title: Baltic states request OSCE meeting with representatives of Belarus
candidate.content:
MINSK - The Baltic states have requested the Polish chairmanship of the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) to hold a meeting with Belarus with regard to military activities in the country.

"Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania requested the Polish OSCE chairmanship to hold a meeting with Belarus and other interested states with regard to unusual military activities," the Polish OSCE chairmanship wrote on Twitter on Sunday.

"The meeting will be convened on Monday in accordance with the Vienna Document," it was said.

The Lithuanian Foreign Ministry said already on Friday that Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia have asked Minsk for a detailed explanation of an unusual military build-up in Belarus.

The Baltic countries "took advantage of the opportunity offered by the Vienna Document on Confidence- and Security-Building Measures (Chapter III: Risk Reduction) of the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe to activate the Mechanism for Consultation and Cooperation as regards unusual Military Activities", the ministry said in a press release.  

"The Baltic states have submitted questions to Belarus about the unusual troop build-up for exercises in the territory of Belarus, the military equipment used, the number of Russian and Belarusian soldiers participating, and the planned return to their usual deployment location", it said.

The questions were sent on February 9 and "Belarus is obliged to provide answers by February 11".

"We urge Belarus to respect its international commitments and to provide information on the nature and scale of the military drills," Lithuanian Foreign Minister Gabrielius Landsbergis said in the press release.

"The avoidance to transparently provide information on the military exercises and the deployment of Russian troops in Belarus in line with the international commitments causes serious concerns over aggressive intentions of Russia and Belarus," he said. 

The risk reduction mechanism of the OSCE Vienna Document is designed to ensure consultation and cooperation among countries to reduce military risks, ensure transparency and prevent military incidents.    

Russia and Belarus on Thursday launched the active phase of a joint military exercise.

Russia's Defense Ministry has said in a press release that the objective of the maneuvers, set to run until February 20, is to "work out the tasks of suppressing and repelling external aggression during a defensive operation".  

Moscow and Minsk have not disclosed how many troops are participating in the drills, but the United States has said Russia has sent some 30,000 troops to several regions of Belarus.

Western countries say Russia has amassed a total of over 100,000 troops along Ukraine's borders in what could be preparations for a potential invasion.

llm_judgement.note: Articles cover different events: Russian-Western talks on security guarantees vs. Baltic states’ OSCE request about Belarusian military activities.
